verdict.rationale: WezTerm is software you install and run on your own machines, including a multiplexer server you can run on remote hosts you control. A runtime probe confirmed `wezterm-mux-server --daemonize` running headless and driven via `wezterm cli`. The pack does not document the openness side of self-hosting: license terms, building from source, or a formal self-hosted server deployment guide. That leaves coverage partial rather than complete. missing for 10: documented open-source license or build-from-source instructions, first-party docs on deploying and operating wezterm-mux-server on your own infrastructure, independent corroboration of self-hosted remote mux deployments

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Multiplex terminal panes, tabs and windows on local and remote hosts
Runs on Linux, macOS, Windows 10, FreeBSD and NetBSD
A connection to a remote wezterm multiplexer made via an ssh connection is referred to as an _SSH domain_.
